items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58865.

With config.active_record.encryption.extend_queries = true, a deterministic encrypted attribute that also declares normalizes silently stops matching rows stored unencrypted (support_unencrypted_data: true) or with a previous scheme's key. The extended uniqueness validation also stops detecting duplicates on case-sensitive collations.

Detail

normalizes wraps the attribute's EncryptedAttributeType in a NormalizedValueType, whose serialize casts before delegating. The extended query support passes previous-scheme values through as AdditionalValues, and only EncryptedAttributeType knew to serialize them as-is. The wrapper instead string-cast the AdditionalValue, normalized it and encrypted the result, so the query's IN (...) contained a value that could never match.

This Pull Request changes:

  • NormalizedValueType#cast now returns an AdditionalValue unchanged when extended queries are installed, so it reaches the encrypted type's existing passthrough.
  • The queried value is cast (and therefore normalized) before previous-scheme values are built, consistent with the value queried under the current scheme.
  • ExtendedDeterministicUniquenessValidator passes the previous-scheme ciphertext as an AdditionalValue, so the normalizer is no longer applied to the ciphertext.

Additional information

I hooked cast rather than serialize on purpose. Prepending serialize onto NormalizedValueType makes serialize_cast_value_compatible? return false, which makes records normalize their values twice when saved (caught by NormalizedAttributeTest#test_minimizes_number_of_times_normalization_is_applied).

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Newly generated tests all use tmp/generators as the destination_root. prepare_destination deletes and recreates the destination_root before each test runs. Multiple tests running in parallel will delete each other's destination_root, causing flaky tests. Two different tests that create the same file in the same directory will also sometimes fail.

Detail

This Pull Request uses a temporary directory for each test to isolate the test run and avoids collisions. Deleting the destination_root can no longer happen in setup because we will no longer have access to the name. It must be handled in teardown.

Additional information

This change is extracted from changes to RubyEvents generator tests - rubyevents/rubyevents#1934
We started off with the default template and ran into quite a few issues before landing on this one.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58862

Manitoba no longer shares winter clocks with US Central time. The existing Central Time (US & Canada) mapping still resolves to America/Chicago, so apps and users treating that name as a proxy for Manitoba will be an hour off every winter.

This follows the same approach as #58321 (for #58316), which handled the equivalent changes in British Columbia and Alberta.

Detail

This pull request adds a friendly zone mapping:

  • Manitoba → America/Winnipeg

Additional information

  • The correct winter offsets for America/Winnipeg also depend on the IANA tz database. Manitoba's change is not included in tzdata 2026d, so it will arrive in a later release. The mapping is needed either way, and the tests only assert name resolution, not offsets, so they don't depend on the installed tzdata version.
  • Unlike other Canadian zones without a friendly name (e.g. America/Whitehorse, America/Inuvik), Manitoba is a whole province whose users have relied on "Central Time (US & Canada)", which will no longer be accurate for them.

items.content_html:
This PR is part of the Rails Foundation documentation project and updates the Autoloading and Reloading guide. The new guide is now open for community review (and it has been reviewed by the author of Zeitwerk, @fxn).

The changes are mainly focused on enhancing the content of the existing guide with further elaboration, spelling things out a bit more and adding examples.

Add Introduction and motivation for autoloading - how constants work in Ruby and why require is needed

Add explanation for how autoloading works

Explain the high level difference between autoloading, eager loading, and reloading up front

Explicitly state the difference between 'main' and 'once' autoloader

Move Eager loading and Reloading further up, as understanding reloading is needed for other sections

Add a note about zeitwerk_enabled? to the Engines section, as it might be most relevant there

Add a code example for autoload_lib_once

Eager loading section: elaborate on what eager_load_all does in the last paragraph. Elaborate on what's the consequence of saying it's "COW-friendly" in the first paragraph.

Reloading section: elaborate that reloading does not "update" an object but rather unloads and then autoloads again. Add the consequence and solution for the "stale object" situation.

Autoloading Without Reloading (autoload_once_paths) section: Explain the MyDecoration example a bit more

New section:

Expanded the last section (Rails.autoloaders) into a new section - How Zeitwerk Interfaces with Rails (inspeired by the [fxn comment](https://3.basecamp.com/3076981/buckets/35498807/todos/9183284516#__recording_10017040619) on the basecamp task).

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

has_one_attached and has_many_attached accept only dependent, service, strict_loading, and analyze, so their generated ActiveStorage::Attachment associations cannot receive other association options such as validate:, deprecated:, collection callbacks like after_add:, or options added by application and gem extensions. The current workaround is to redeclare the association, duplicating its internal scope, class_name, as:, inverse_of:, and dependent: :destroy settings and relying on Active Storage internals.

Detail

Both macros now accept **options and pass them only to the attachment association, not the blob through association. The options come last so they can override Active Storage’s defaults. This mirrors delegated_type forwarding extra options to belongs_to. Unknown options still raise, through has_one or has_many option validation rather than the macro’s keyword arguments.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Combining a callable value_method with a selected or disabled Proc raises TypeError in collection select helpers. Both options are supported individually. For example, a collection_select with computed option values and a predicate that disables unavailable records fails while rendering the form.

This also reproduces directly with:

options_from_collection_for_select(
  [1, 2],
  ->(number) { number },
  :to_s,
  ->(number) { number == 2 }
)

The second option should be selected. Instead, extract_values_from_collection passes the value Proc to public_send and raises TypeError.

Detail

Use the existing value_for_collection helper when extracting selected and disabled values, matching the way option values are rendered. This supports callable values while preserving public_send behavior for method names.

Add regressions for callable values combined with selected and disabled Procs, plus a collection_select example that verifies computed values, model selection, and disabled options together.

Additional information

Reproduced against rails/rails main at 2cc9c08699bc8062c0851dab772cbea64affabda using Ruby 3.4.7.

  • Before the fix: all three new tests raise the expected TypeError.
  • After the fix: all three pass.
  • Full Action View suite: 3,285 tests, 7,437 assertions, no failures, errors, or skips (cd actionview && PARALLEL_WORKERS=1 bin/test).
  • RuboCop passes for both changed Ruby files.

Searched open and closed Rails issues and PRs for the helper, value methods, and Proc selection/disabled combinations; found no matching report. Related PR #57163 documents callable value/text methods but does not address this combination.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because SecureRandom.base32 (added in #56288) is meant for one-time codes that people read and type by hand, but its alphabet still contains 0 and 1. Crockford's Base32 handles 0/O and 1/I/L confusion at decode time by treating the lookalikes as equal. Rails only generates these codes and doesn't provide a decoder, so apps usually compare them as exact strings. A user who types O for 0 (or I/L for 1) gets rejected unless each app adds its own normalization.

Detail

This Pull Request changes SecureRandom.base32 to SecureRandom.base30, which also leaves out 0 and 1. The alphabet is now 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ. None of 0, O, 1, I or L can appear, so codes can't be misread, even in typefaces where those characters look alike, and no decoding rules are needed.

SecureRandom.base30     # => "FYWCJTEVA78KM8C3"
SecureRandom.base30(24) # => "SVE9HA8Q3SXE5AVB63JMNVGS"

base32 hasn't been released yet (it's only on main, planned for 8.2), so this renames it instead of deprecating it. The CHANGELOG entry and the 8.2 release notes are updated to match.

Additional information

Each character now carries log2(30) ≈ 4.91 bits instead of 5, so a 16-character code has about 78.5 bits of entropy instead of 80. For short human-entered codes, avoiding misreads seems worth that small cost.

cc @monorkin @miharekar, the authors of #56288.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58834. Follow-up to #50020.

db/schema.rb on PostgreSQL carries schema qualifications that no migration would ever write.

Every extension whose objects live outside the current schema is qualified, even when the schema is fixed by the extension's control file and cannot be picked with CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA:

enable_extension "pg_catalog.plpgsql"
enable_extension "tiger.postgis_tiger_geocoder"

Replaying the second line with SCHEMA tiger requires the schema to exist, so loading a fresh database fails with PG::InvalidSchemaName: schema "tiger" does not exist, while a plain CREATE EXTENSION postgis_tiger_geocoder would have created tiger itself. Keeping an extension's schema off the search path is a legitimate layout: the PostGIS tiger geocoder itself went from adding tiger to the search path, to asking users to add it, to making it optional [1][2][3].

And once more than one schema is dumped, every table and enum type is qualified too, so adding an extension's schema to schema_search_path turns create_table "posts" into create_table "public.posts" throughout the file.

Detail

  • Qualify an extension with its schema only when that schema was picked at CREATE EXTENSION time, through the SCHEMA clause or the default creation schema, i.e. when the control file does not fix it.
  • Qualify tables and enum types only when they are outside the current schema, as extensions and enum_types already do. An unqualified name loads into the current schema, which is where it was dumped from; loading therefore depends on the loading connection's schema_search_path, as it always has for single-schema dumps.

For extensions with a fixed schema and for tables in the current schema this restores the Rails 8.0 output. An extension installed with CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA, such as enable_extension "heroku_ext.pgcrypto", and tables in other dumped schemas are dumped as before.

Before, with schema_search_path: public, postgis (extensions are dumped regardless of the search path, so tiger appears too):

  create_schema "postgis"

  enable_extension "pg_catalog.plpgsql"
  enable_extension "postgis.postgis"
  enable_extension "tiger.postgis_tiger_geocoder"

  create_enum "public.mood", ["happy"]

  create_table "public.posts", force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

After:

  create_schema "postgis"

  enable_extension "plpgsql"
  enable_extension "postgis.postgis"
  enable_extension "postgis_tiger_geocoder"

  create_enum "mood", ["happy"]

  create_table "posts", force: :cascade do |t|
    ...
  end

Additional information

  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.

[2] https://gitea.osgeo.org/postgis/postgis_tiger_geocoder/src/tag/2025.2/README.md
[3] https://gitea.osgeo.org/postgis/postgis_tiger_geocoder/commit/e79704e1eb99fe36a316db26ff907cb2d0fe1396

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

When a tracked variant is first processed, Active Storage currently publishes its variant record before uploading the image. A failed upload leaves a record that marks the variant as processed, preventing regeneration. Concurrent requests can also observe the record before its image is available.

Related to #55088.

Detail

This change does not alter when variant processing starts: lazily processed variants are still generated on first use. Once processing begins—whether lazily, immediately, or in a background job—upload the image before creating or finding its variant record. The record therefore remains an availability marker for a successfully uploaded variant.

Delete uploaded files on transaction rollback, and defer enqueuing purge jobs for failed or unused blobs until the enclosing transaction commits.

Add regression tests for upload visibility, retry after failure, rollback cleanup, record creation failures, and deferred purging. A concurrency test uses two threads with separate SQLite connections and synchronization barriers to verify that both callers resolve to the same variant record and only the losing upload is purged.

Additional information

Validation on Ruby 4.0.5:

  • Full Active Storage suite: 618 tests, 1919 assertions, no failures or errors.
  • Four MuPDF tests skipped because mutool is unavailable.
  • S3/GCS service tests were not enabled because credentials were unavailable.
  • JavaScript lint/build consistency check passed.
  • RuboCop passed for both changed Ruby files.
  • git diff --check passed.
  • The concurrency regression test fails against the implementation before this fix.

Checklist

  • This PR contains one related change.
  • The commit explains what changed and why, with a related issue reference.
  • Regression tests are included.
  • The Active Storage changelog is updated.

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58844, #58845, #58846 and #58847; this PR is the last layer of the
stack and its diff is only the final commit.

Motivation / Background

ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility applies adapter-specific behavior
through connection.adapter_name checks, so a third-party adapter has to patch
the version classes to participate, and a subclass of a bundled adapter (one
reporting "CockroachDB", for example) never matches the exact-string check
even though it builds on the parent's schema statements.

Supersedes #58162, split into #58844, #58845, #58846, #58847 and this PR.

Detail

The connection adapter resolves a migration's declared version to a
CompatibilityBehavior subclass through compatibility_behavior_for, and
Migration#method_missing routes every schema operation through it. A behavior
covers its own version and older, adjusts arguments and calls super; nested
TableDefinition modules cover t.<op> calls. An adapter without the hook gets
the no-op base behavior.

The PostgreSQL and MySQL adjustments move into per-adapter behaviors; no
adapter_name checks remain in compatibility.rb. SQLite3 has none left after
#58845, and the explicit proper_table_name call #58846 added to
V5_1#change_column goes away because behaviors receive the table name with
table_name_prefix and table_name_suffix already applied.

Two details when reading the diff:

  • V5_0 marks the default: nil it injects for integer primary keys so the
    MySQL behavior can drop the injection without touching a user-written
    default: nil.
  • The verbose message is built at the execution point so it shows options as a
    behavior executes them; table names still display as written.

Additional information

Migrations on the bundled adapters produce the same schema and verbose output
as before: the DDL emitted for the affected operations, captured for every
version from 4.2 to current on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL, is identical before
and after this change.

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58846.

Motivation / Background

Seven ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility version classes (V8_0, V7_0,
V6_1, V6_0, V5_2, V5_0 and V4_2) define the same private method:

def compatible_table_definition(t)
  t.singleton_class.prepend(TableDefinition)
  super
end

Each one exists only to prepend that class's own TableDefinition module, and
a new version class with a TableDefinition module has to repeat it.

Detail

Replaces the seven overrides with one ancestor walk in
Migration::Current#compatible_table_definition: it prepends the
TableDefinition module of every version class among the migration's
ancestors, oldest version first, so the newest version's module ends up first
in method lookup, the same order the chained super calls produced. A version
class now only declares its module.

No behavior change. The migration compatibility tests exercise the
TableDefinition modules across versions and pass unchanged.

Additional information

The seven overrides accumulated one version class at a time:

  • 214dc7d - V5_0 and V4_2
  • 57015cd (#34970) - V5_2
  • e8437a6 (#38717) - V6_0
  • 867d27d (#41084) - V6_1
  • da472b6 (#43904) - V7_0
  • 489e08d (#55086) - V8_0

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58845.

Motivation / Background

With config.active_record.table_name_prefix = "p_", a migration declaring
5.1 or earlier that changes a column with :default, :null or :comment on
PostgreSQL applies the type change and those options to different tables:

class AddDefaultToPostsTitle < ActiveRecord::Migration[5.1]
  def change
    change_column :posts, :title, :string, default: "untitled"
  end
end
ALTER TABLE "p_posts" ALTER COLUMN "title" TYPE character varying
ALTER TABLE "posts" ALTER COLUMN "title" SET DEFAULT 'untitled'

The second statement fails if no posts table exists, and silently changes an
unrelated table if one does.

Migration#method_missing applies proper_table_name before an operation
reaches the connection, but Compatibility::V5_1#change_column applies
:default, :null and :comment in separate statements by calling the
connection directly, with the table name as written in the migration.

Detail

Applies proper_table_name to those statements as well, so the migration
above runs:

ALTER TABLE "p_posts" ALTER COLUMN "title" TYPE character varying
ALTER TABLE "p_posts" ALTER COLUMN "title" SET DEFAULT 'untitled'

As in method_missing, it is not applied during revert: the CommandRecorder
replays the recorded command through the migration, which applies it then.

  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]

items.content_html:
Stacked on #58844.

Motivation / Background

On SQLite, a migration declaring 6.0 or earlier that asks for a reference type
other than integer gets an integer column anyway:

class AddUserToPosts < ActiveRecord::Migration[6.0]
  def change
    add_reference :posts, :user, type: :bigint
  end
end
ALTER TABLE "posts" ADD "user_id" integer

Migration::Compatibility::V6_0#add_reference forces type: :integer on
SQLite. The SQLite3 adapter already defaults references to integer while
honoring an explicit type, so the override only discards the type the
migration asked for.

Detail

Removes the SQLite branch from V6_0#add_reference. The migration above now
runs:

ALTER TABLE "posts" ADD "user_id" bigint

The existing 6.0 tests keep asserting the integer default for references
without an explicit type; a new test asserts that an explicit type: :bigint
is honored.

The verbose migration output no longer shows type: :integer for these calls,
since the adapter now supplies the default instead of the compatibility class;
the resulting column is the same.

Additional information

  • 99eea87 (#43295) added the branch to fix #43168: after e8437a6 (#38717)
    made V6_0#add_reference build a ReferenceDefinition itself, the SQLite3
    adapter's integer default was bypassed, so re-running a 6.0 migration under
    6.1 turned a references column from integer into bigint and changed
    schema.rb. The fix targeted that default case.
  • 7c5a8fc (#42350) routed V6_0#add_reference through super, which reaches
    the adapter's default again. It removed the matching SQLite3::TableDefinition
    module for t.references but left this branch behind.
  • Since then the branch has had no effect on the case it was added for:
    removing it on main leaves every migration compatibility test green on
    SQLite, and the 11 tests that execute the branch all call add_reference
    without type: and get an integer column from the adapter either way.
  • Its only remaining effect was discarding an explicit type:, which is what
    this PR fixes and covers with a test.

  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility applies adapter-specific adjustments
through connection.adapter_name branches, such as the ENGINE=InnoDB default
in Migration[5.1] on MySQL and the timestamp type for :datetime in
Migration[6.1] on PostgreSQL. Most of those adjustments have no test asserting
the schema they produce, so a regression in any of them would go unnoticed.

Detail

Adds tests for the adjustments, asserting the resulting column types, defaults,
comments and table options rather than the code path:

  • MySQL: Migration[5.1] create_table injects ENGINE=InnoDB and keeps a
    user-written options:; Migration[7.0] change_column keeps an explicit
    collation:.
  • PostgreSQL: Migration[5.0] id: :uuid defaults to uuid_generate_v4()
    while an explicit default: and Migration[5.1] keep the current default;
    Migration[6.1] add_column and change_column map :datetime to
    timestamp while Migration[7.0] does not; the Migration[5.1]
    change_column :comment follow-up; ActiveRecord::Schema[6.1] applies the
    same version compatibility during a schema load.
  • Verbose output shows table names as written under table_name_prefix,
    including the second name of rename_table and remove_foreign_key.

Each test fails when the adjustment it covers is disabled.

Additional information

Tests only, no behavior change.

Motivation / Background

Fixes #58838.

where(attr: nil) always emitted IS NULL, even when normalizes ..., apply_to_nil: true turns nil into a non-nil value such as "". On a NOT NULL column that query matches nothing, and where.not(attr: nil) matches every row.

Detail

If the attribute type has a normalizer, QueryAttribute#nil? now uses the normalized database value. nil that normalizes to "" queries as name = '', same as where(attr: ""). A normalizer that maps blank to nil still queries with IS NULL.

Motivation / Background

Prepared statements promise a significant performance gain.

This Pull Request has been created because many statements are marked as unpreparable in Rails: many methods in Arel or elsewhere use SqlLiteral under the hood, which automatically mark the Arel collector as not preparable. This should be configurable.

Detail

This Pull Request changes Arel::Nodes::SqlLiteral so it can opt-in to being preparable. The resulting changes in the ToSql Visitor are implemented and aliases built by AliasPredication#as as now considered as preparable.

Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

items.content_html:
Followup #51951

cc @jeremy @tenderlove @tomrossi7

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because process: cannot vary per record, while the preprocessed: option it replaces could.

#51951 introduced process: with three static modes and deprecated preprocessed: for removal in Rails 9.0. But preprocessed: accepts a Symbol or a Proc called with the record:

attachable.variant :thumb, resize_to_limit: [4, 4], preprocessed: :should_preprocess?

There is no equivalent under process:, so an application that decides per record has
no migration path and has to keep calling the deprecated option — and will lose the behaviour entirely in 9.0.

My use case is the following : I have a Document model that has_one_attached :file with variants. and belongs to polymorphically to an attachable, and I have a strategy / variant per "attachable, for some I want them lazy while others need the later strategy.

Detail

This Pull Request changes ActiveStorage::NamedVariant#process so that, along with :immediately, :later, and :lazily, the :process option also accepts a Proc or the name of a method on the record. Either one is called with the record and returns one of the three modes:

class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_one_attached :avatar do |attachable|
    attachable.variant :thumb, resize_to_limit: [100, 100],
      process: ->(user) { user.public_profile? ? :later : :lazily }

    attachable.variant :medium, resize_to_limit: [300, 300],
      process: :medium_process_mode
  end

  def medium_process_mode
    public_profile? ? :later : :lazily
  end
end

Additional information

A value that doesn't resolve to a mode now raises ArgumentError, with the same wording as the existing :analyze option. Previously an unknown symbol was returned as-is and silently behaved like "never process

Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

items.content_html:
I am sharing this PR for early feedback on my approach. Do y'all think this is a good high-level architecture to pursue?

About the boot performance, as discussed in Hakodate, I'd be interested to look in what it would take to support precompiling templates with Bootsnap, making parsing performance less important. - @byroot https://x.com/_byroot/status/2052666788446412954 (May 8, 2026)

Problem

Rails compiles templates the first time they are rendered in each process, causing cold-render times to be higher, most evident when an application is regularly deployed/booted. Introducing Herb to Rails exacerbates this problem, as Herb template compilation is roughly an order of magnitude slower than Erubi:

Template Size Erubi Herb Added Ratio
Tiny 58 B 3.9 µs 28.3 µs +24 µs 7.2x
Small 250 B 10.4 µs 116.1 µs +106 µs 11.2x
Medium 1 KB 24.4 µs 365.6 µs +341 µs 15.0x
Large 3 KB 81.7 µs 1,059.7 µs +978 µs 13.0x

At GitHub, we use @jhawthorn's https://github.com/jhawthorn/actionview_precompiler to shift this work to boot time (I've opened a PR to upstream it into core: #57234). However, with the introduction of Herb, compiling our templates at boot time more than doubled, an unacceptable increase in our production environment.

Proposed solution

This PR introduces a build-time cache for erb template handler output (but could be expanded to all handlers). In testing, it brought Herb to be more or less in line with Erubi at boot time:

Handler Cache Time
Erubi Off 15.138s
Erubi On 13.118s
Herb Off 25.167s
Herb On 13.335s

Cache loading costs about 0.177s.

  • Erubi: cache improves median by 13.2%.
  • Herb: cache improves median by 47.9%.
  • With cache enabled, Herb adds only 1.5% to median time.
  • Without cache, Herb is 69.1% slower.

To be clear, this PR does not provide the same performance improvements as actionview_precompiler. It only serves to eliminate the added overhead of using a slower ERB handler such as Herb.

Alternatives considered

I looked at adding this functionality to bootsnap, but found that template compilation needs the Rails application to be booted which is something bootsnap does not currently do.

Future work

We could eventually incorporate pieces of actionview_precompiler into this caching step.
items.title: [DO NOT MERGE] Add cache for erb template handler output
